newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to sell stake in Sukhoi Log gold firm.
newsitem.headline: Russia to sell stake in Sukhoi Log gold firm.

text.p: Russia will tender in March a 49 percent stake in a unit of Lenzoloto, the company which holds the right to develop Russia's giant Sukhoi Log gold field, an aide at the Natural Resources Ministry said on Thursday.

"A 49 percent stake in the joint-stock company Sukhoi Log (a unit of Lenzoloto) will be offered in March, and the tender is open to everyone, including foreigners," said the aide to First Deputy Natural Resources Minister Boris Yatskevich, who is also chairman of the board at Lenzoloto.
He said that Sukhoi Log, in the Irkutsk region in southeastern Siberia, was the former Soviet Union's and possibly the world's largest untapped gold field.
He put its reserves at 1,100 tonnes (about 35 million troy ounces) and said the field also had large but unspecified amounts of palladium.
"We have had to make public the size of the reserves; otherwise no investor would be interested," he said.
The joint-stock company Sukhoi Log would retain a 51 percent stake in any venture to mine the gold, he said.

He said that the 49 percent stake to be tendered was valued at the high end of hundreds of millions of U.S. dollars, and possibly as high as $1 billion. He could not provide details on the terms of the tender.
Star Mining Corporation NL of Australia nominally holds a 31 percent stake in Lenzoloto, which is a mining company, he said.
